results.final_feedback: Candidate faithfully encodes the COMPLETE COMPLEX_READINESS contract with the ship target, authoritative owner paths, all declared operands and results, canonical datatypes and units, and no unauthorized formula execution or invented evidence checks.

Candidate faithfully encodes the ship-owned operands, average-pressure formula with expected-result-scaled tolerance, Table 3 lookup relationships and evidence, exact category-to-factor mapping, and exact propagation of the selected factor to the ship.

Candidate faithfully encodes the COMPLEX_READINESS boundary: it targets ships, validates every linked structural member without requiring member existence, and requires the declared operands and result on their authoritative owner with correct quantity datatypes and units.
No candidate is a canonical IACS UR I2 Table 8 row or required-grade controlled value; the available field, case, and lookup terms cannot substitute for the absent bounded row/grade values.

Candidate is semantically faithful and deterministically valid. It targets ships, applies only when the declared design ice condition is thin first-year ice with possible old-ice inclusions and category A is absent, and reports violations when category B is missing or any non-B category is present, thereby enforcing category B exclusively without imposing unconditional property existence.

Rewrite the bounded envelope constraint so coverage failures are violations: the current FILTER(?coveredWaterlines = ?requiredWaterlines) suppresses evaluation and accidentally passes whenever an intended-waterline or LIWL segment is missing at a critical longitudinal position. Preserve breakpoint, segment-interior, crossing, and shared-domain coverage using the existing owner paths and SHACL Core presence/datatype/metre checks, without OPTIONAL inside FILTER NOT EXISTS. Remove the invented 1e-6 relative/fallback constants and use only an approved tolerance scaled from the expected envelope value, not the reported LIWL value; do not use exact equality. No vocabulary matching is needed.
